name: Change Verb in -Ize

1.definition: Forms a verb for causing or undergoing a change connected to the adjectival base.

projection.target: In the transparent causative use stable specifies a result. The -ize family also has noun bases and lexicalized meanings beyond this construction.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Verbs ending in -ize
curious.summary: Adding -ize to an adjective can make a verb meaning to cause or undergo a change tied to that adjective.
curious.body:
Stable is an adjective, and stabilize is a verb. In The update should stabilize the connection, the verb means to make the connection stable. The adjective names the result of the change.

The -ize ending is also added to nouns, and some -ize verbs have meanings of their own that go beyond this pattern. This dictionary's pattern is the one built on an adjective, where the verb means causing or undergoing a change connected to that adjective. The analysis is provisional. The pattern is also written with the spelling -ise.
curious.try: Think of an adjective, such as stable, and add -ize. What would the new verb mean?

teacher.summary: Helps explain verbs like stabilize formed from an adjective with -ize or -ise.
teacher.explain: The pattern forms a verb from an adjective base plus -ize (or -ise), meaning to cause or undergo a change connected to the adjective. In the transparent causative use, the adjective stable specifies the result of stabilize. The -ize family also has noun bases and lexicalized meanings beyond this construction, so the adjective's contribution may not be transparent. This dictionary links this pattern to the causative-inchoative entry and marks the analysis as provisional.
teacher.terms: Traditional grammars may call -ize a verb-forming suffix. This dictionary treats the pattern as a morphological construction from an adjective.

contrasts.text: The update should stabilize the connection.
contrasts.note: The verb causes the connection to become stable.

watch_for: A learner might assume every -ize verb comes from an adjective, when some have noun bases.
A learner might assume the meaning of every -ize verb follows from its base.
teacher.activity: Give students adjectives (stable, final, legal). They form verbs with -ize if the verb exists, write a sentence for each, and check each in a dictionary to see whether the result matches the adjective's meaning.

checked.note: Fixed: curious body no longer says this dictionary covers only the transparent-result case (the entry defines the pattern as a change connected to the adjective; transparent result is the causative use); 'causative-inchoative alternation' changed to 'entry'; 'derivational' changed to 'morphological' as in the entry.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Change Verb in -Ize." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/deadjectival-ize-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, 5c11b28).
